question: The Chairman Mr. Mokbul, distributes flour from the godown of Union Perishad at dark night after hearing the cry of hungry children. Moreover he took along his wife for helping the childbirth women. Abeda, sister of the Chairman, thinks the Muslim scholars play vital role in medical science beside Islamic knowledge, modern medical science is indebted to them. [1766933122363]

Give logic in favour of your opinion.","marks":4,"answer":"Yes, I agree with Abeda's comment as it highlights the contribution of Muslim thinkers to medicine.
The contribution of Muslims to medicine is remarkable. The contribution of Muslims is at the root of the development of modern medical science. Among those through whose contribution medical science has reached the pinnacle of development are Ibn Sina, Abu Bakr Al Razi, Ibn Rushd, Hasan Ibn Haytham etc. This point is noticeable in Abeda's statement.
In the stem, Abeda's comment is - Muslims have contributed a lot in the field of medicine. Modern medical science owes a great deal to them. In her speech, the contribution of Muslims in the field of medicine is highlighted. In fact, Muslims have been remembered in various fields of medicine. Al Razi was the greatest physician of his time. He introduced new doctrines in the treatment of measles, neuroctric etc. Another notable name in medical science is Ibn Sina. He is known as the founder of modern medicine and surgery. His authored 'Al-Qanun Fit-Tibb' is famous as the Bible of Medicine. In addition, many other Muslim thinkers have contributed to the field of medicine by writing books on medicine.
So, it can be said that modern medical science owes a lot to the medieval Muslims in the field of medicine. So, the comment of Abeda in this regard is correct.

question: Salam and Kamal are two public representatives. After being elected, Salam called the people and said brothers, as long as I follow Allah and his Rasul (sm.) you will follow me and corrects my mistakes. On the other hand, Kalam distributes the aid received from the government equally among the relatives nonrelatives, the rich and the poor. [1766933122666]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Madina Sanad?","marks":1,"answer":"Hazrat Muhammad (Sm) created a written document after consulting with the leaders of all tribes of Madinah and this written document is called the Charter of Madinah."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Ibn Sina called the pioneer of surgical treatment?","marks":2,"answer":"Ibn Sina is regarded as the pioneer of modern surgery, medicine and techniques of treatment because of his outstanding contribution in the field of medicine. Ibn Sina was a philosopher, physician, mathematician, astronomer as well as a famous scientist of the Muslim world. He is regarded as the pioneer of modern surgery, medicine and techniques of treatment. By writing the book 'Qanun Fit Tib' he introduced modern surgery to the world. Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In Salam's speech, the first Khalifa of Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr's (Ra.) speech is reflected.
Among the adult Muslims, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first to have embraced Islam. He was the most dedicated server of Islam. Before the demise of Rasul (Sm) he always kept himself busy in serving Rasul (Sm) and Islam. He accepted the Quran and Sunnah as his life's best ideal. That is why he was given the role of Khalifa after the demise (632 A.D.) of Rasul (Sm). After becoming the Khalifa, he took oath to always follow the instructions of Allah and His Rasul (Sm). This ideal of Abu Bakr (Ra.) is reflected in Salam.
After being elected as the people's representative, Salam called all the people and said, 'You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm). And if I tread the wrong path, you shall rectify me.' Similarly, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.), who was democratic minded, addressed the crowd after being elected as the Khalifa of the Muslim world and said, 'You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm). And if I tread the wrong path, you shall rectify me.' In his speech, the features such as loyalty to Allah and Rasul (Sm), democracy and giving importance to people's opinions were revealed. And representative Salam is cherishing the characteristics of Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) who is the exemplary ruler of all time."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the activities of the great man which are found expression in the deeds done by Kalam.","marks":4,"answer":"Kalam's activities reflect the equal humanity and the noble qualities of Hazrat Umar (Ra.).
The second Caliph of Islam, Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was an epitome of justice. He did not make any distinction between friend and foe in establishing justice. There was a wonderful combination of hardness and tenderness in his character. As he was strict for truth and justice, he felt pain for humanity. People's suffering tormented him. So, he made every effort to relieve their sorrow. Kamal followed this great ideal.
In the passage it is seen that as a public representative, Kamal believes in equality and humanity. He distributed the aid received from the government equally among the rich and the poor, friend and foe. Also, he wandered around the neighborhoods late at night to realize the suffering of the people. The same characteristic can be observed in the character of Hazrat Umar (Ra.). He was a democratic, humanist, and neutral ruler. He used to distribute the wealth received from BaytulMaaI equally among all. In this case, he did not do any distinction between the rich and the poor, and friend and foe. On the other hand, as a benevolent ruler, he used to roam about alleys and lanes in the cover of darkness to see for himself the conditions of the people. On hearing the cry of hungry children he personally carried flour to their house. He took along his wife to a nomad's tent to help a nomad woman in her childbirth.
In the end, it can be said that Hazrat Umar (Ra.) was a great example of equality and humanity. He has been exemplary in history as an ideal ruler by establishing accountable governance and ensuring the welfare of the people. Public representative Kalam has partially captured these ideals.
---"}]

parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"Who was Buhaira?","marks":1,"answer":"Buhaira was a priest during the Prophet's (Sm.) time. He prophesied about the Prophet (Sm.) being the Akihiri Nabi (Last Prophet) of the final phase."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"How was Mecca conquered? Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"The great Prophet (Sm.), along with ten thousand followers, advanced towards Makkah in the month of Ramadan on the 8th Hijri. The Prophet (Sm.) pitched his tent at a short distance from Makkah. The Quraish were struck with fear at the sight of the Muslim camp. Through this, it is proved that the truth's victory is inevitable."},{"label":"C","letter":"C","text":"Khatib saheb’s statement is in accordance with which speech of Islam? Explain it.","marks":3,"answer":"The speech of Khatib Saheb is consistent with the epoch-making speech of Islam known as the farewell Hajj sermon.
In the tenth Hijri year, in 632 CE, the great Prophet (Sm.) performed Hajj in the company of more than 1 million Sahabis. As it was his last Hajj, it is known as the "Farewell Hajj". This contains adequate guidance on all issues pertaining to humanity. This guidance has been reflected in the speech of Khatib Saheb.
Khatib Saheb said, "Be kind to wives and subordinates; do not exaggerate religion." The great Prophet (Sm.) also said the same to warn mankind. We know our women are mothers. They are also creations of Allah. This is why wives have similar rights over men as men have over them. Hence, men have to behave decently with their wives. The great Prophet (Sm.) also advised to be very conscious of the subordinates. Their rights cannot be denied. He said, "Feed and dress them as you feed and dress yourselves. If any of them commits any unpardonable crime, set him or her free, but you shall not maltreat them. For they too are human beings identical to you, very much Allah's creation. All Muslims are brothers of one another, and you are tied to a common brotherhood." He also warned not to commit excess in matters of religion, as many preceding nations became extinct for that. Hence, the speech of Khatib Saheb is similar to the sermon of the Prophet's (Sm.) farewell Hajj."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":"Analyze the teachings of Union Chairman Zahid saheb by identifying which caliph’s character his statement resembles.","marks":4,"answer":"The first Caliph Abu Bakr's (Ra.) character resembles the teachings of Union Chairman Zahid Saheb.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first to embrace Islam among adult Muslims. He was a dedicated servant of Islam. He was always engaged in the Prophet's (Sm.) service until his death, as well as Islam's service. He held onto the Quran and Sunnah as the best ideals of life. After the Prophet's (Sm.) death in 632 CE, he took on the responsibility of Khilafat. He took an oath on his election as Khalifah to follow Allah and His Rasul's (Sm.) guidance. This example has been reflected in Zahid Saheb's speech.
Chairman Zahid Saheb stated to the union, "You will follow me and help me as long as I follow Allah and His messenger." Likewise, the democratic-minded Hazrat Abu Bakr addressed the Muslim nation on his election as Khalifah: "You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm.). And if I tread the wrong path, you will rectify me. Those poor among you are really strong to me as long as their rights are not restored. And those who are strong, they are weak before me till the share of the rightful claimants is not realized from them". Such a speech indicates obedience to Allah and His Messenger (Sm.) as well as democracy by giving importance to public opinions, etc. So, the exemplary ruler of all time, Hazrat Abu Bakr's (Ra.) characteristic, is nurtured by Chairman Zahid Saheb.
In conclusion, it can be said that Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) is the ideal for all rulers. A part of his character has been revealed in the speech of Chairman Zahid Saheb.
---"}]

And disputes were imposed unfairly. At such a time a stranger established an organization called 'Sabuj Sangha' to set peace in the area. As a result, disputes and quarrels in the society stopped. [1766933123637]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is meant by Ideal of Life?","marks":1,"answer":"Activities of great man which are followed to make life perfect and successful are called ideals of life."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":"Why is Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) called the savior of Islam? Therefore, it can be said that the description of the book read by Mr. Rafiq can be compared to the society of Ayyam-i-Jahiliyah."},{"label":"D","letter":"D","text":""The Sabuj Shanghai" established by the stranger is similar to which activity in the life of the Holy Prophet (Sm.)? After seeing the horror of the war of Fiza, peace-loving Prophet Muhammad (Sm) was deeply and extremely disturbed. Thus, he formed Hilful Fuzul with other peace-loving youths, which is a peace organization. In its ideals, the Arab tribes of that time stopped quarreling and established peace and harmony. Finally, it can be said that the organization named Sabuj Sangha, founded by the newcomer, is similar to Hilful Fuzul, established by Rasul (Sm), as its objective is to establish peace in society.

question: Being elected as the Mayor, Mr. Adnan played a great role in establishing justice. One day, he came to know that his elder son Afnan drank wine mixing with some stalkers. Immediately, he gave his son sever punishment. On the other hand, his younger son Aitck passed HSC successfully this year. When he was asked by his father about future plan, he said, "I want to be a physician like a great physician who had great contribution in different fields of science in the middle age and who is considered to be the pioneer of modern surgery." [{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is Haqqul Ibad?","marks":1,"answer":"Haqqul Ibad is the rights of Allah's servants."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":""Hilful Fazul paved the way to U.N.O"-Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"“Hilful Fuzul paved the way to U.N.O.” this statement is correct.

One day he got to know that his elder son Afnan had drink alcohol along with the boys of the area. Immediately he brought his son under strict punishment. Muslim contributions to medical science are unforgettable. They are at the heart of modern medical science. Al-Razi is one of them. He was the greatest physician, scientist, and surgeon. He has been indicated by the speech of Abdul Alim.
The ideal whom Abdul Alim wants to follow to be a doctor is the greatest Muslim medical scientist. He is still remembered as a surgeon. This is true in the case of Al-Razi only, as he was the greatest medical scientist. His goodwill and fame spread in all directions. In the domain of surgery, Al-Razi was the greatest person of his time. His surgical technique was superior to that of the Greeks. In all, he wrote about 200 books. Of them, about one hundred are on medical subjects. He wrote a book on small-pox measles named ‘Al-Judariwal Hasbah’. Medical experts were struck with awe in view of its originality. Another book by him bears the title ‘Al-Mansuri’. It is written in 10 volumes. These two books have immortalized him in medical science. He introduced new theories on the treatment of measles, pediatrics, neuropsychiatry, etc. In his work Al-Mansuri, he mentioned such diverse topics as anatomy, physiology, the brain, medicine, principles of hygiene, dermatology, cosmetic items, surgery, poison, fever, etc.
Therefore, we can understand from the above discussion that Abdul Alim wanted to be a medical scientist, following Al-Razi. His contribution to medical science is incomparable.

question: Nawshad is a young social worker. One day, there arose a possibility of bloody clash between two groups of his village on the issue of the establishment of a library. Giving a balance verdict with prudent, he saved the villagers from an inevitable bloodshed. Because of his such contribution in social welfare, villagers elected him chairman of three village. At the inaugural speech, he advised them to appreciate the messages of historical speech of Prophet (Sm.) and also said, "That speech contains all round dictations for whole mankind" [1766933128459]
parts:
[{"label":"A","letter":"A","text":"What is 'Charter of Madinah'?","marks":1,"answer":"Hazrat Muhammad (Sm) created a written document after consulting with the leaders of all tribes of Madinah and this written document is called The Charter of Madinah."},{"label":"B","letter":"B","text":""Conquest of Makkah is the shining example of Prophet (Sm.)’s forgiveness." The Quraish of Makkah signed the Hudaibiyah Treaty with the Holy Prophet Muhammad (Sm) and the Muslims in the 6th Hijri year. On their violation of the treaty, Rasulullah (Sm) advanced toward Makkah with 10,000 followers in 630 AC. The Quraish were stuck with fear at the sight of the Muslim camp. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) was the greatest ruler of the world. He established good governance based on justice. He established peace and order in the society by conducting judicial work with discretion and impartiality. Which can be seen in Nawshad's activities.
Nawshad's work is similar to an incident during the Prophet's (Sm) youth. When the Holy Prophet (Sm) was 35 years old, the Kaaba Sharif was reconstructed. On the 9th of the month of ZilHajj of the tenth Hijri (632 AD), the Holy Prophet (PBUH) gave a historic speech at Arafat ground in Makkah as an adequate guidance for the conduct of life for mankind. It is known as the 'Farewell Hajj Speech' as the last Hajj of the life of the Holy Prophet (PBUH). In this speech, he gave general advice to Muslims and mankind to be guided in the right direction. Establishing equality irrespective of caste, not exaggeration with religion, kind behavior towards wives were some of the important advices of this speech. Meyor Noman Saheb's statement represents this.
The mayor of the stem said in his speech that everyone is equal regardless of caste and clan and not to exaggerate religion. His speech like this is a reflection of the ideals of the Prophet's (PBUH) Farewell Hajj speech. In this speech, the Holy Prophet (PBUH) said, "Remember, all Muslims are equal irrespective of land, colour, tribe and community. Right from this day tribal superiority is obliterated. All Muslims are brothers of one another and you are tied into a common brotherhood", He also said, "Do not commit excesses in matters of religion; many preceding nations became extinct for that. So, it can be said that Meyor Noman's speech is similar to the prophet's (PBUH) Farewell Hajj speech.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Evaluate the contribution in Islam of that Khalifa with whom the speech of Mr. Kamal similar to.","marks":4,"answer":"Mr. Kamal's statement is similar to that of the first Khalifah of Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.), who contributed immensely to the service of Islam.
The possessor of democratic belief and thinking, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) said to the people after being elected Khalifah of the Muslim world, "You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm). And if I tread the wrong path, you shall rectify me". You will correct me immediately." Such ideals can also be found in Mr. Kamal's speech.
Mr. Kamal of the stem said, you shall obey and follow me as long as obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm). In his speech, the reflection of the speech of Abu Bakr (Ra.) has emerged. Abu Bakr's (Ra.) contribution to the service of Islam is immense. Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first of the older men to embrace Islam. During the battle of Tabuk he donated all his property. After being elected Khalifah, he addressed the people and established the Oneness of Allah, democracy and accountable governance. He protected Islam and Muslims from chaos by resisting the suppression of the false prophets and the deniers of Zakat.
So, it can be said that Abu Bakr (Ra.) was a devoted soul for Islam. We should be inspired by his ideals and devote ourselves to the service of Islam and country.

Explain.","marks":3,"answer":"In Mr. Mostofa's speech, the speech of the first Khalifah of Islam, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was revealed.
Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) was the first among the elderly men to embrace Islam. He was a devoted servant of Islam. Before the death of Rasul (PBUH), he devoted himself to the service of Rasul (PBUH) and Islam. He accepted Quran and Sunnah as the best ideals of life. So, after the death of Rasul (PBUH) (632 AD), he was entrusted with the Khilafat. After assuming the Khilafat, he took an oath to administer the Khilafat according to the instructions of Allah and the Messenger (PBUH). The reflection of his ideals can be seen in Mr. Mostofa.
Being elected as a representative, Mr. Mostofa called the people of the area and said, "If I obey Allah and Rasul's (PBUH) orders, you will follow and support Me. If I do the opposite, you will correct me." In the same way, Hazrat Abu Bakr (Ra.) who had a sense of accountability, after being elected as the Khalifah of the Muslim world, said to the people, "You shall obey and follow me as long as I obey Allah and His Rasul (Sm). In his speech, the characteristics of showing loyalty to Allah and Rasul (PBUH), accountability and giving importance to people's judgment of good and bad have been revealed. Hazrat Ali (Ra.) was a man of valour and extraordinary strength. Hearing his name used to create terror in the hearts of the infidels. Rasul (PBUH) presented him with the 'Zulfiqar' sword for his extraordinary bravery in the Battle of Badr. He did not hesitate to accept any situation in life for the Prophet (PBUH). And this matter is revealed in Mojahar.
In the stem, Mojahar was awarded the "Sword of Honour" for his heroic contribution as a soldier and risk his life to bring peace to the country.This attitude of him represents the ideal of Hazrat Ali (Ra.). Basically Ali (Ra.) always devoted himself to the Holy Prophet (PBUH).
When Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) migrated to Madinah, he left Hazrat Ali (Ra.) in charge of his trust and left him on his bed. He performed this duty duly despite the grave risk of his life. He considered the value of his life insignificant compared to the responsibility given by the Holy Prophet (PBUH). Responsibility was his prime concern.
There are very few young men who have staked their lives on the path of truth like Hazrat Ali (Ra.). We will also be devoted to the path of truth and establish truth.
